Outline · not written yet

This is the planned structure of the chapter, published so the curriculum can be reviewed before the prose is written. Each heading below becomes a section; the last section is what you will build and test. About 75 minutes when written.

10.1 · The judge is a measuring instrument

agreement with human labels, by slice.

10.2 · Its error rates, measured

false-positive and false-negative rates against a gold sample.

10.3 · Correcting the estimate

Rogan–Gladen for a judged pass rate, derived.

10.4 · Prediction-powered inference

PPI and PPI++: a few human labels plus many judged ones, with valid intervals.

10.5 · Where to spend human labels

budget allocation and active selection.

10.6 · Drift

re-validate on a schedule, because the judge and the traffic both move.

What you build

Rogan–Gladen and PPI++ estimators, with a simulation proving interval coverage. Every number it produces is asserted by a test, and the chapter's companion notebook recomputes it.
